name_reason: Follows fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> convention; no address residue. The 'fade_in' in the name refers to the cinematic itself (its ANI frames render their own fade-in); the wrapper does set-palette-full + render-cinematic + fade-OUT-to-black. This caller-intent rationale is documented in both src comment and Ghidra plate, and the name is established (sole caller fd2_play_ending_and_record_clear, 3 sites). Accurate and conventional -> keep.
purpose: Wrapper that loads a cinematic image palette, applies it at full brightness, plays its ANI animation sequence, then fades the screen to black.
logic_summary: If palette_idx != -1: memset mode-13h framebuffer 0xA0000 (64000 bytes) to 0, then load FDOTHER.DAT[palette_idx] palette into data_fd2_vga_palette_data_ptr (palette_idx == -1 keeps the current palette). Then fd2_set_vga_palette_range(0,0xFF,0) applies the palette at full brightness (3rd arg is darken-amount, 0 = none). Then fd2_play_ani_file_animation_sequence(anim_idx, per_frame_delay, 0) renders the cinematic. The body then physically falls through at 0x1f882 into fd2_play_palette_fade_to_black, which ramps darken 0..0x3F (fade-OUT to black, 0x40 steps via the shared loop body at 0x1f503-0x1f524) and RETs (that RET also returns from this function). Modeled in src as a direct tail call fd2_play_palette_fade_to_black() (a real separate function with 22 callers). The __CHK(0x10) prologue is a compiler-injected stack probe.
signature: void __cdecl fd2_load_and_fade_in_cinematic_image(uint32 anim_idx, uint32 per_frame_delay, uint32 palette_idx)
